title: Tell the reader which pipeline roles are enabled; target briefs to them
summary: The reader brief gains an "Enabled roles" section built from the effective config (reader, producer, verifier always; planner and critic only when [job_plan] enabled is true), plus a tenth reading rule that brief content targets only enabled roles. Goal: stop readings from putting new content into planner/critic briefs when job planning is off; the audience is the reader agent and the maintainers who redirect it by hand.

defaults_applied.how: Change is Rust code and tests.
New tests plus cargo test and clippy criteria.
Tests assert the brief output names the enabled roles, not just that fields exist.
One focused change in the brief builder and its caller.
Gives the reader the config fact so it stops guessing roles, rather than patching one reading.
Rule marked prose only; the role list itself is derived from config by code.
Criteria check the rendered brief for enabled and disabled roles.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (ReaderInputs at ~2214, READING_RULES at ~2247 as a [&str; 9], reader_brief at ~2276, tests near ~4511-4590 that assert READING_RULES.len() == 9) and crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (read_once builds ReaderInputs at ~567 from jc.config) and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (JobPlanConfig.enabled, default false; job_plan is an Option). Entry point: read_once -> reader_brief. The role list is computed from jc.config.job_plan in read_once and passed as a new ReaderInputs field. No record or data file is added under crates/, so the records allow-list is not touched.

Enabled roles: reader, producer and verifier always run; planner and critic are listed only when config.job_plan is Some and enabled is true. 'hard' mode still counts as enabled; the section may note the mode. The effective config is the already-merged jc.config.
The new rule is prose only (no check_* refusal): it adds no refusal, so no refused-readings percentage applies. It is added to READING_RULES with the count constant and existing count tests updated.
The reader prompt token budget (3 left) is unaffected: changes are in Rust brief text rendered at run time, not in the prompt files.
athena.toml and defaults.toml are not changed; only read for the current [job_plan] enabled = true.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs builds a reader brief with job planning disabled and asserts the brief names reader, producer and verifier as enabled roles and does not list planner or critic as enabled; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
A second test builds the brief with job planning enabled and asserts planner and critic appear in the enabled-roles section; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.

A test in crates/athena-core (e.g. reading.rs tests) shows read_once/reader input construction derives the role list from the config's [job_plan] enabled value, not a hard-coded list; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs READING_RULES contains a new rule stating that brief content targets only enabled roles, marked `(prose only)`, and the array length and existing length assertions are updated consistently.
reader_brief output has a heading section listing the currently enabled roles, checkable by Grep of the heading constant in briefs.rs.
No unrelated behavior changes: `cargo test` passes with all existing tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

out_of_scope: Changing planner, critic, producer or verifier briefs or prompts
Making the rule a refusal check (check_*) in athena-core
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml or the [job_plan] settings
